title: Retain bounded replay completion and AgentGov error evidence

requirement.summary: Extend the test-only Codex proposal replay normalizer so an exact tool completion and allow-listed AgentGov structured error cannot collapse back to call_started.

objective.rationale: The live replay proved exact invocation but the current summary omits completion presence and ignores the structured AgentGov error contract, preventing honest layer attribution.

goal: Add privacy-bounded completion counts/statuses and normalized AgentGov tool-error evidence to the test-only replay reducer while preserving existing exact-call, form, success-result, terminal, and raw-data exclusion behavior.
non_goals: Do not run a Codex turn, model request, external replay, direct App Server probe, or form interaction.
Do not change AgentGov Core, the MCP Adapter, protocol, proposal schema, native form, task-admission semantics, configuration, installed runtime, release identity, or architecture.
Do not retain raw error messages, tool arguments, text content, model messages, reasoning, credentials, source content, absolute paths, metadata, usage, or arbitrary extension fields.
Do not infer the historical replay's missing completion or error from new fixtures.
Do not commit, push, publish, release, deploy, merge, or mutate a consumer repository.
acceptance_signals: Every exact proposal-tool item/completed event contributes a deduplicated completion count and an allow-listed completion status even when its result is absent or unrecognized.
A structurally valid agentgov.mcp-tool-error exposes only contract, error code, matching proposal-tool stage, bounded field path, rule, and retryable flag; raw messages and extensions are discarded.
A completed item with a structured AgentGov tool error resolves to call_failed rather than call_started, while a completed unknown result has an explicit completion_unknown state.
Existing exact successful proposal results, native forms, terminal state, unrelated-event rejection, and privacy exclusions remain covered and compatible.
Documentation states that the correction improves future evidence only and cannot reconstruct or reclassify the already discarded historical replay events.
validation_commands: python -m unittest tests.test_replay_event_normalizer tests.test_governance_mcp tests.test_public_documentation_freshness tests.test_user_documentation tests.test_task_contract -v

items: Retaining too much error material would violate the replay privacy boundary.
Changing state precedence could misclassify a form or successful result when multiple exact calls occur.
New deterministic fixtures cannot establish what happened in the historical replay after its raw events were discarded.

stop_conditions: Stop before any raw error/message retention, historical replay reinterpretation, model or external call, form response, Adapter/protocol/config/install change, or product implementation.
Stop if the evidence state cannot remain deterministic for multiple call IDs, duplicate events, forms, and terminal ordering.
Stop before any Git action, publication, release, deployment, merge, or consumer mutation.

decision.rationale: On 2026-08-09, the privacy-bounded evidence correction completed. Future summaries retain deduplicated completion count/status, explicit unknown completion, and at most eight strictly validated AgentGov error records while raw material remains excluded. Eleven dedicated tests, 72 focused tests, and the 758-test full baseline passed with two platform skips. Historical replay evidence remains unchanged; any replay or product change requires a separate product-owner decision.
